research_method.claude: SLR following PRISMA; 8 digital libraries searched November 2024 + 35 studies from prior review + 30 expert additions + backward snowballing; quality assessment (Reporting, Rigor, Credibility, Relevance); Elicit-assisted extraction; coding with the in-IDE HAX taxonomy; open coding of 250 future-work statements; 90 studies
research_method.nlm: SLR following PRISMA; 90 studies included from 257 identified / 223 screened; in-IDE HAX taxonomy (Impact, Design, Quality); Elicit-assisted extraction with human verification; research agenda of 17 topics x 10 methodology types
research_method.value: Systematic literature review following PRISMA; database search (November 2024) plus studies from the authors' prior review, expert-informed additions and backward snowballing; quality assessment; extraction supported by Elicit with manual verification; 90 primary studies coded with the in-IDE HAX taxonomy (Impact, Design, Quality); open coding of 250 future-work statements into a research agenda (17 topics, 10 methodology types)
research_method.note: Claude flags minor count inconsistencies in the paper (257 vs 256 identified; 19 vs 16 educational studies).

context.claude: Mixed; 90 primary studies, professional (71/90) and educational (19/90) contexts
context.value: academic (secondary/review); 90 primary studies on AI assistance inside IDEs (71 professional, 19 educational contexts)

ai_discussed.note: Human-AI experience with AI coding assistants in IDEs is the review topic (GitHub Copilot in 36/90 studies); Elicit also used for extraction.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not specified by either; 'remote' appears only for remote vs in-person study sample sizes.

cat_productivity.note: Task completion speed and productivity gains synthesized (up to 55.8% faster; 26–35% gains); productivity is the largest future-work cluster (43).

cat_quality.note: Quality dimension: correctness, security vulnerabilities, readability, maintainability of AI-generated code.

cat_collaboration.note: Trust is trust in the AI tool (classed under attitudes/satisfaction by both), not team collaboration.

cat_satisfaction.note: Thin: perceived mental workload and self-efficacy of novices, trust/reliance (both extractors class these as satisfaction/well-being); no satisfaction measure as such.

cat_activity.note: Thin: suggestion acceptance rate (labelled Activity by both) and edits, recommended alongside time on task; no repository activity metrics.

cat_devex.note: DevEx framework not used (Claude: not reported; NotebookLM: referenced); 'DevEx' labels on workload/trust are generic.

cat_agile.note: Waterfall model used only to categorize SDLC stages.

cat_survey.note: Synthesizes perceptual evidence (trust, perceived workload, self-efficacy) and survey-based studies (12/90).

evidence.quote: It applies a formal Systematic Literature Review (SLR) process, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework (Moher et al., 2010).
it includes 90 papers identified through a multi-step procedure that combines database search, backward snowballing, and expert-informed additions.
In November 2024, after finishing the planning phase, we searched the aforementioned sources, using titles, keywords, and abstracts as the basis for our queries.
We included studies first available between January 2022 and November 2024, including preprints on arXiv.
This work was conducted manually by the first author, with support from an AI-based system called Elicit
To address RQ3, we analyzed 250 future work statements extracted from the reviewed papers
The studies analyzed in this review represent two primary contexts for working with AI in software development: professional (71 out of 90) and educational (19/90)

For instance, participants using GitHub Copilot completed implementation of an HTTP server in JavaScript up to 55.8% faster than control groups (Peng et al., 2023), while other investigators observed productivity gains ranging from 26% to 35% for complex tasks
When using AI tools, verifying suggestions, refining prompts, and reworking code generated by AI might take up to 50% of developers' time (Mozannar et al., 2024a).
Across studies, quality is examined from multiple perspectives, including code correctness, security, and readability.
Time-pressured studies report lower mental workload and steady self-efficacy with assistance
Novices complete tasks more quickly and report lower workload when the use of in-IDE AI is structured, yet they are vulnerable to subtle errors and may overtrust suggestions
Evaluate the effect beyond time spent on the task by reporting acceptance, edits, and verification effort.
Among 90 papers reviewed in this study, 12 employed a survey methodology, 32 followed an experimental design, and 38 utilized qualitative methods.
